lyrics:
[Intro: pounding piano riff, horn stabs, talk-box voice]
Area code love
(Where you from? Throw it up)

[Verse 1: first rapper, booming and relaxed]
Touchdown, wheels on the ground, back in the place
Where the corner store man still remembers my face
Same cracks in the court, same bend in the rim
Same old-timer on the stoop, and I wave at him
Been around the world on a ticket and a dream
Ate in rooms where the forks come in teams
But nothing hits like a plate from the truck
Paper napkin, hot sauce, and a dollar for luck
Roll the windows down, let the summer in
Every block's got a story and a next of kin

[Chorus: talk-box sings, crowd shouts the answers]
Area code love
(Where you from? Throw it up)
Area code love
(Three little numbers, say them loud)
We keep it rocking
From the block to the back yard
Area code love

[Verse 2: second rapper, faster and brighter]
Now my auntie's on the porch with a pitcher and a fan
Cousin on the grill with a spatula in hand
Kids on the bikes doing circles in the street
DJ in the driveway with the trunk for a seat
I left with a bag and a busted phone
Came back with a kid and a little bit of chrome
They put a coffee shop where the barber used to be
But the bass from that Chevy still belongs to me
So lift your cup if you ever had to roam
And you still know the way that the streetlights take you home

[Chorus: talk-box sings, crowd shouts the answers]
Area code love
(Where you from? Throw it up)
Area code love
(Three little numbers, say them loud)
We keep it rocking
From the block to the back yard
Area code love

[Bridge: roll call, both rappers trading, claps on every beat]
From the two-oh-six to the three-oh-five
Three-one-two, keep the party alive
Seven-one-three and the four-oh-four
Two-one-three kicking in the door
Nine-oh-seven and the eight-oh-eight
If I missed your code, go ahead and celebrate

[Final Chorus: talk-box and full crowd, horns on top]
Area code love
(Where you from? Throw it up)
Area code love
(Three little numbers, say them loud)
We keep it rocking
From the block to the back yard
Area code love

[Outro: talk-box alone, piano riff fades]
Home, home, home
Area code love
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 92 BPM, 4/4, G minor. A rolling, bouncing West Coast party groove. Loud, generous, sunlit.

VOICE: Two male rappers with different tones: the first deep, booming and relaxed, the second higher, quicker and more excitable. The hook is sung through a talk-box, a guitar-effect tube that makes a synthesiser 'speak', so it sounds robotic and soulful at once. A crowd shouts the bracketed answers.

INSTRUMENTS: A pounding, two-handed acoustic piano figure that repeats all the way through. Punchy horn section stabs. Fat, sliding synth bass. A high, whining sine-wave synth lead. Heavy drums with a hard clap on the backbeat. Wah guitar scratches. Party crowd noise.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the piano riff, horn stabs and the talk-box hook once. 0:16 Verse 1, ten lines. 0:58 Chorus 1. 1:19 Verse 2. 2:01 Chorus 2. 2:22 Bridge, the area-code roll-call over claps and piano, both rappers trading lines. 2:47 Final chorus with horns and the whole crowd. 3:18 Outro, the talk-box sings alone over the piano riff, fading by 3:50.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-90s G-funk: huge clean low end, bright piano, vocals dry and upfront, everything wide.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first talk-box line over the piano at 0:05.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The narrator has been gone for twenty years and notices what changed (a coffee shop where the barber was) and what did not. The hook never names a place, so the anthem belongs to any town.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Arrival, celebration, a moment of noticing, then the roll-call.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

Somebody lands back in the place that made them, after a long time away, and the whole neighbourhood comes out. Then the roll-call starts.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: any home town at all, since the hook never names one; a reunion; a road-trip song; or a team anthem. Listeners wait for their own three digits.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: the place as the star, a talk-box hook, a pounding piano figure with horn stabs, and a roll-call that makes people wait for theirs. Designed mishearing: through the talk-box 'area code love' is heard as 'are you cold, love?' and 'every code, love'.
